_doc: Revert-verify mutant for the IN-JEST half of issue #4444: after dropping `process.exit(0)` from `remove-property`'s success path, every success axis asserts `expectNaturalExit` (exit was never called) instead of `toContain(0)` / `toEqual([0])` / `toBe(0)`. That predicate is what keeps the fix from being silently reverted by a future edit — restoring the exit reddens the axes below. ⚤ The DELIVERED-bytes half cannot live here (jest mocks process.stderr.write and process.exit, so no pipe and no flush is exercised — integration-test-revert-verify §A66); it lives in dryrun-4444.removeproperty.spec.json. Same shape as set-body-4436.guard.spec.json, which locked the equivalent predicate for `set-body` in #4443. Expectation written BEFORE the run. ⛔ HONEST LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: every remove-property suite uses PROSE test names, so no per-test id can be extracted (integration-test-revert-verify §A47 — the axis NAME is the machine key, and a red_re that finds nothing reports 'красных 0', i.e. a FALSE 'does not differentiate'). The key here is therefore the SUITE itself, which is coarser: it pins that the mutant reddens this suite, not WHICH of its ten tests. That is still falsifiable and still extractable — the driver's control run must leave it GREEN — and it is strictly better than leaving the in-jest half with no mutant at all. Seven of this suite's assertions are the migrated success axes, so the mutant reddens it through them.

M1_process_exit_restored._note: Restores process.exit(0) at the end of the success path. Every migrated success axis asserts that NO exit was recorded, so all of them redden at once — which is the point: the predicate is a ratchet against the exit coming back, not a per-scenario check.
